date_note: The ministry's announcement was reported on 23 November and the pages give no earlier day; the operations ran over the previous 5 days, with no calendar dates given.
exec: Turkish authorities report arrests over phishing-site fraud and unauthorised access to company systems to obtain internal documents and personal data.
plain: Turkey's Interior Ministry says cybercrime operations in 12 provinces over 5 days caught 101 suspects; 60 were arrested. Cases covered phishing fraud, illegal betting, child abuse images and breaking into company systems.

key_findings: The Interior Ministry said operations in 12 provinces over the last 5 days caught 101 suspects; 60 were arrested and 34 placed under judicial control.
Operations were coordinated by the national police cybercrime department, MASAK and chief public prosecutors' offices.

Offences named: child sexual abuse material, illegal betting and gambling and its advertising, fraud through phishing sites, and unauthorised access to company systems to obtain internal documents and personal data.
recommendations: The reports give no guidance for organisations or the public.

summary: Turkey's Interior Ministry said cybercrime operations in 12 provinces over the last 5 days caught 101 suspects, of whom 60 were arrested and 34 placed under judicial control, DHA and Anadolu Agency reported. The cases covered child sexual abuse material, illegal betting, fraud through phishing sites, and unauthorised access to company systems to obtain internal documents and personal data.
title: Turkey: Interior Ministry says 60 arrested after cybercrime operations in 12 provinces

validation.note: Corroborated by DHA (dha.com.tr) and Akşam (aksam.com.tr, carrying Anadolu Agency's report): two independent agencies that each relay the Interior Ministry's announcement with the same figures. The ministry's own post was not read.
